applicable_failures: Candidate set came from /tmp/candcompact.txt, an earlier-stage filtered list. The strict script only scanned matters in that file, so matters outside it were never scanned. This is the follow-up filter dropping matters pattern.

The agent's second and third calls grep and sed the same /tmp/strict_hits.txt for a hand-picked list (1001-00003, 1001-00004, 1010-00004, 1022-00004, 1033-00005, 1037-00006, 1038-00009). That list narrows the set before review. Many hit matters, such as 1009-00001, were never opened as documents.

The script printed 2070 hit lines and about 55k characters of output, plus about 130k characters from the sed reads. This is heavy and risks flooding context. The agent then judged matters from snippets only.
critique.concerns: The scan was limited to the earlier candidate list, so the "complete 90-matter set" claim depends on how that list was built. Six matters were named from snippets alone, and the L&E practice-area status of each was not verified. The sed ranges were chosen by line number rather than by matter, so some hit matters were probably never reviewed. Dozens of matters with hits remain unopened.
critique.recommendation: Check how many matters strict_hits.txt covers and compare that with the full store. Produce a per-matter summary of hit counts and the best snippet, with no cap on matters. Then check each matter's practice area and open the key acceleration document in every matter with equity-tied acceleration hits.

Common failures at this stage in past runs:
- An uncapped store-wide scan with broad or common terms printed snippets for every match, producing millions of characters that filled the context before any response was written.
- A store-wide scan timed out or printed nothing after reaching only part of the store, and the agent accepted the partial output instead of narrowing by matter range or folder, rerunning, or searching file names, so qualifying matters never entered the candidate set.
- A scan had already surfaced every needed matter, but a follow-up filter on file names, folder names, exact phrases, or a hand-picked list silently dropped matters whose documents were named or worded differently.
- Matters were listed in file-name searches or scan output, but later scripts restricted to certain names or folders so the needed matter was never opened or examined.
What successful runs did: Passing runs also hit timeouts, but their output stayed bounded enough to read, and they often split the scan into parallel matter-range scripts or narrowed to a key acronym or per-matter hit counts, then picked candidates from what was reached.
Reconsider before moving on. If the goal was not fully reached, or any failure above applies, reopen this stage now: call stage_start with stage="Scan document text with an extraction script" and a goal that says what you will fix. Otherwise call stage_start for the next stage you need.
